# Popup

Popup: a small panel of secondary content anchored to a control, text or a short list and never a form.

Also asked as: popover, flyout, inline dialog.

**Import:** `import { Popup } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/overlays-and-layering/Popup/Popup.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/overlays-and-layering/Popup/Popup.stories.jsx` — Layout, Content, InteractionStates, Overview, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Open, PlacementTop, PlacementBottom, PlacementLeft, PlacementRight, WidthSmall, WidthMedium, WidthLarge, BodyOnly, TriggerClick, TriggerHover, TriggerFocus, TriggerHoverAndClick

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/overlays-and-layering/Popup/Popup.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Popup` for a small panel of secondary content anchored to a control: a
definition, a preview or a short list. Its body is text or a short list, never a
form. For a form, use a `Modal`. It holds more than a `Tooltip` and
less than a `Modal`, and unlike a modal it does not take the page.

`trigger` is the element it hangs off, `children` the body, `title` the optional
title. `triggerType` is `click` (the default), `hover`, `focus`, an array of
those, or `manual` for a popup you drive with `show`.

It is the Popups pattern's Popup: one surface padded 16, with the title in
heading.xsmall over the body, and no arrow. `width` picks the tier, `sm` 320
(the default), `md` 400 or `lg` 480. It opens 4 from its trigger and never
comes nearer than 8 to the screen's edge.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title it with a short noun phrase: "Session 12". | Title it with a sentence or a question. |
| Write the body in one or two sentences, or a short list. | Write a paragraph or put a form in the body. |
| Name the trigger for what it opens: "What is this?". | Name the trigger "Click here" or "More". |
| Keep the popup to supporting detail. | Put the only copy of something the user needs in it. |

## Best practices

### Dismissal is on by default, except when you own the state. {#dismissal-is-on-by-default-except-when-you-own-the-state}

```jsx
// A click away and Escape both close it — `rootClose` defaults to true for
// every trigger but `manual`.
<Popup trigger={<Button appearance="primary" text="Details" />} title="Session 12">…</Popup>

// With `manual` the caller owns `show`, so nothing dismisses it but the caller.
// Pass rootClose explicitly if you want the outside click to reach onToggle.
<Popup trigger={<Button appearance="primary" text="Pinned" />} triggerType="manual" show={open}
       onToggle={setOpen}>…</Popup>
```

### A string trigger is a button. {#a-string-trigger-is-a-button}

```jsx
// Fine — a string trigger renders a real <button className="plus-popup-trigger">,
// which carries the role, its own text as the accessible name, and Enter/Space.
<Popup trigger="What is this?">…</Popup>

// Also fine, and what you want when the trigger needs a Button's own styling.
<Popup trigger={<Button appearance="subtle" text="What is this?" />}>…</Popup>

// Incorrect — a `div` is not a control. `aria-expanded` is not added to it,
// because a state on something with no role is invalid ARIA. Pass a control
// instead of decorating a div.
<Popup trigger={<div>What is this?</div>}>…</Popup>
```

Do: A string trigger becomes a real button, named by its own text.
Don't: A div is not a control: it has no role and no keyboard behavior.

### Hover alone leaves out the keyboard. {#hover-alone-leaves-out-the-keyboard}

`triggerType="hover"` has no keyboard equivalent. Use `['hover', 'focus']` at
least, and `click` when the content is more than a sentence — hover content that
must be read is content that has to stay put while it is read.

### Keep the body short, and keep forms out. {#keep-the-body-short-and-keep-forms-out}

Do: A short noun phrase for the title and one sentence for the body.
Don't: A question for a title and a paragraph for a body.

### Name the trigger for what it opens. {#name-the-trigger-for-what-it-opens}

Do: Says what is behind it.
Don't: Says nothing about what opens, and reads as nothing in a list of links.

## Accessibility

- **The trigger announces the popup.** It carries
  `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and an `aria-expanded` that tracks the open state —
  including while the caller drives `show` themselves. Both are applied only to
  a trigger that can hold them: a `button`, an `a`, a `Button`, anything you
  have already given a `role`, and the button a string trigger becomes. A plain
  `div` gets neither, because a state on something with no role is invalid ARIA.
- **`aria-controls` is not set.** It needs the rendered panel's id,
  `id` is optional here, and an `aria-controls` pointing at an element that does
  not exist yet is worse than none.
- **Opening it by a click or a key moves focus into it.** Focus lands on the
  first focusable element inside, or on the popup itself when there is none, so
  a keyboard or screen reader user starts where the content is. A popup opened
  by hover leaves focus where it was. Closing it with Escape or a click away
  returns focus to the trigger.
- **Escape and a click away both close it.** Both come from the same
  `rootClose` binding, which is on for every trigger but `manual`.
- **Do not put required content in one.** Anything the user must read to finish
  the task belongs on the page. A popup is an aside.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `trigger` | node (required) | — | The element that triggers the popup. A plain string becomes a real `button`. |
| `children` | node (required) | — | The popup's body content. |
| `title` | node | — | Popup title |
| `label` | string | — | Names the popup for assistive tech when there is no `title`. Falls back to the trigger's own accessible text when neither is given. |
| `placement` | enum | `'top'` | Popup placement |
| `triggerType` | string or arrayOf | `'click'` | Trigger behavior |
| `defaultShow` | bool | `false` | — |
| `show` | bool | — | — |
| `onToggle` | func | — | — |
| `container` | object | — | Where the popup portals to. Defaults to the page, or the modal the trigger sits in. |
| `offset` | array | — | — |
| `rootClose` | bool | — | Dismiss on a click outside. Defaults to true for every trigger but `manual`. |
| `width` | enum | `'sm'` | The width tier: sm 320 (default), md 400 or lg 480. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`placement`** — `auto` · `top` · `bottom` · `left` · `right` · `top-start` · `top-end` · `bottom-start` · `bottom-end` · `right-start` · `right-end` · `left-start` · `left-end`

**`width`** — `sm` · `md` · `lg`

Anything not listed is not a valid value.

## Related

- For one line of help on a control, use `Tooltip`.
- For a decision that must be made before continuing, use `Modal`.
- For detail that belongs with the content rather than over it, use `Accordion`.
